encyclopedia.summary: Gonzo's 2006 adaptation of Tatsuhiko Takimoto's novel. A young man who dropped out of university and shut himself in is pulled out by the girl next door and starts touching society again. It treats shut-ins and internet culture as comedy, but by the second half anxiety and delusion cover the screen.

key_facts.value: Tatsuhiko Takimoto's novel Welcome to the N.H.K.

highlights: Turns the lead's delusions into the image itself, blurring reality and fantasy.
Self-mocking comedy shifts into panic and isolation in the back half.
It is one of the few works to take 2000s Japanese discourse on otaku and shut-ins head on.

encyclopedia.summary: Naoko Yamada's 11-episode 2021 adaptation of the medieval war chronicle The Tale of the Heike, made at Science SARU. Biwa, a girl who can see the future, lives inside the fall of the Heike clan while knowing how it ends. The original's sung cadence is carried into the animation's rhythm, and the family's collapse is followed through her eyes.

Biwa's sight turns the series into something watched with the ending already known.

encyclopedia.summary: OLM adapted Yasuki Tanaka's manga into 25 episodes in 2022. Shinpei returns to his island hometown, dies in an accident, and wakes on the same day again, and the island's old case keeps folding into his family's secret. The repeating day is used as a way to re-examine the characters' choices, not only as a mystery device.
highlights: Each pass through the same day changes the island's relationships, and what refuses to change becomes the clue.
Shadows and framing carry the pressure of the loop.
The back half is re-staged on screen clearly enough for readers of the manga.
